problems.title: Focus and directrix of a parabola
problems.question: A=(0,1/4), and B lies on y=x². Find a horizontal line whose distance from B equals AB for every B.
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
formulas: Let B=(t,t²). AB²=t²+(t²−1/4)²=(t²+1/4)².
steps: Thus AB=t²+1/4, exactly B’s vertical distance from y=−1/4.

problems.title: Range of a function plus its absolute value
problems.question: f has range [−1,1]. Find the range of f+|f|.
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
formulas: t+|t|=0 for t≤0 and 2t for t≥0.
steps: As t traverses [−1,1], the output traverses [0,2].

problems.title: Coinciding monotonicity intervals
problems.question: For which a does ax²+6x+11 have the same increasing interval as the decreasing interval of 3x²+2ax+199?
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
formulas: The second interval is the left half-line ending at −a/3. The first must open downward, a<0, with endpoint −3/a.
steps: Set −3/a=−a/3, giving a²=9.
Retain the negative root.

problems.title: A parallelogram with equal area and perimeter values
problems.question: A nonrectangular parallelogram has one side 3 cm; its area and perimeter have the same numerical value. Which listed second side is possible?
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
formulas: 3b sinθ=2(3+b), and sinθ<1 because it is not a rectangle.
steps: The necessary and sufficient condition is 2(3+b)<3b, or b>6.
Among 5,3,2,7,4,6, only 7 qualifies; sinθ=20/21 gives a nonright angle.

problems.title: Area from the smallest and largest diagonal triangles
problems.question: The four triangles formed by a trapezoid’s diagonals have minimum area 4.5 and maximum area 8. Find total area.
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
formulas: The other two triangles each have area √(4.5·8).
steps: Each mixed area is √36=6.

problems.title: Maximum-area sector of fixed perimeter
problems.question: A sector has perimeter 12, counting two radii and the arc. What radius maximizes its area?
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
formulas: Arc length=12−2r; area=r(12−2r)/2=9−(r−3)².
steps: The maximum occurs at r=3.
The corresponding arc is 6 and angle is 2 radians, a valid ordinary sector.

problems.title: Roots on opposite sides of two bounds
problems.question: Find a for which (x−14)²=ax−2 has one root below 9 and the other above 19.
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
formulas: For f(x)=(x−14)²−ax+2, both 9 and 19 must lie strictly between the roots.
steps: The stronger condition is a>3; then both sign conditions ensure the required root locations.

problems.title: Even natural terms of a recurrence
problems.question: a₁=0.25 and aₙ=2aₙ₋₁+1. How many terms are positive even integers?
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
steps: The first terms are 1/4,3/2,4,9,19,… .
The third is even. Every later term is twice an integer plus 1, hence odd.

problems.title: Count vertices from two diagonals
problems.question: In a regular even-sided polygon, the angle between a shortest and a longest diagonal from one vertex is 60°. How many vertices?
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
formulas: The longest diagonal is a diameter; the shortest skips one vertex. Their angle is 90°−360°/n.

problems.title: Sum ten triangle areas in arithmetic progression
problems.question: Nine rays divide a triangle into ten parts with base lengths in arithmetic progression. The middle two areas are S and Q. Find total area.
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
formulas: Shared height makes the areas an arithmetic progression too.
steps: The average of an even number of arithmetic terms is the mean of its middle pair.
Total=10(S+Q)/2.

problems.title: A nested radical raised to the eighth power
problems.question: Given $a=\sqrt[3]{199}$ and $b=\sqrt[4]{a\sqrt[3]{a\sqrt a}}$, find $b^8$.
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
formulas: The exponent of a inside b is (1+(1+1/2)/3)/4=3/8.
steps: Thus b⁸=a³.
Since a is the cube root of 199, a³=199.

problems.title: Compare four quadratic inequalities
problems.question: Which are equivalent: I x²+2x−8≤0; II (x²+1)(x+4)/(x−2)≤0; III |x+1|≤3; IV (x−2)(x²+x+1)/(x+4)≤0?
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
formulas: The factors x²+1 and x²+x+1 are strictly positive.
steps: I and III both give [−4,2].
II gives [−4,2), excluding its denominator zero. IV gives (−4,2], excluding its denominator zero.

problems.title: Which powers are rational?
problems.question: a=199¹ᐟ²+199³ᐟ², b=199¹ᐟ³+199⁴ᐟ³, c=199¹ᐟ⁴+199⁵ᐟ⁴. Which of a²,b³,c⁴ are rational?
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
formulas: Factor out the smallest power: a=200·199¹ᐟ², b=200·199¹ᐟ³, c=200·199¹ᐟ⁴.
steps: Squaring, cubing and taking the fourth power give 200²·199,200³·199,200⁴·199.
All three are integers.

problems.title: A vector parallel to a line
problems.question: Which listed vector is parallel to 6x−9y+13=0?
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
formulas: A direction vector (u,v) satisfies 6u−9v=0.
steps: Each other listed vector gives a nonzero value.

problems.title: Distance from a midpoint to a line
problems.question: In rectangle ABCD, AB=12,BC=8. K is midpoint of BC and M midpoint of CD. Find distance from K to AM.
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
steps: Then K=(12,4),M=(6,8), and AM has equation 4x−3y=0.

problems.title: Sum floors of forty arithmetic terms
problems.question: a₁=1,d=0.25, bₙ=floor(aₙ). Find b₁+⋯+b₄₀.
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
formulas: aₙ=1+(n−1)/4, so each integer 1 through 10 occurs four times as a floor.

problems.title: Two simultaneous congruences
problems.question: How many two-digit natural x satisfy x≡3 mod4 and x≡4 mod5?
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
formulas: The simultaneous class is x≡19 mod20.
steps: Its two-digit representatives are 19,39,59,79,99.

problems.title: Sum only terms above one
problems.question: A geometric progression has b₁=512,q=−0.5. Find the sum of terms greater than 1.
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
formulas: Only its positive odd-index terms can qualify.
steps: They are 512,128,32,8,2; the next positive term is 1/2.
Their sum is 512+128+32+8+2.

problems.title: Greatest distance between two circles
problems.question: A is on (x+5)²+(y−5)²=25 and B on (x−5)²+(y−5)²=9. Find the greatest AB.
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
formulas: The greatest distance is center distance plus both radii.
steps: Centers (−5,5),(5,5) are 10 apart; radii are 5 and 3.
The extreme points on the center line attain 10+5+3.

problems.title: A dot product from triangle sides
problems.question: AB=6,BC=12,AC=8. Find vector AB·AC.
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
formulas: AB·AC=(AB²+AC²−BC²)/2.
steps: The value is (36+64−144)/2.

problems.title: Two divisor-labeled dice
problems.question: A natural n has six positive divisors, which label each of two fair dice. Find the probability the product equals n.
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
formulas: For each divisor d on the first die, exactly one second label n/d works.
steps: There are 6 successful ordered pairs out of 36 equally likely pairs.

problems.title: A probability measured by an annulus
problems.question: Independent uniform x,y are chosen in [−2,2]. Find P(1<x²+y²<4).
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
formulas: The sample square has area 16; the event is the annulus of radii 1 and 2.
steps: The full annulus lies in the square and has area π(4−1)=3π.
Divide its area by 16; boundaries have probability zero.

problems.title: Mean and median of arithmetic data
problems.question: A finite nonconstant arithmetic progression is used as data, with mean a and median b. What must hold?
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
formulas: Symmetric terms sum to first+last.
steps: The mean is (first+last)/2.
For odd term count the middle term has that value; for even count the middle pair’s mean has that value.

problems.title: Two side and altitude sums coincide
problems.question: Two sides sum to 199, and their corresponding altitudes also sum to 199. What must the triangle be?
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
formulas: For included angle C, the altitudes are b sinC and a sinC.
steps: Their sum is (a+b)sinC=199sinC.
Since the given sum is 199, sinC=1, so C=90°.

problems.title: Similar triangles with a constant side increment
problems.question: Each side of a triangle is 2 greater than the corresponding side of a similar smaller triangle. The smaller area is 4√3. Find the larger area.
problems.idea: Apply the stated rule, keeping all special cases.
formulas: If scale factor is k>1, (k−1)a=(k−1)b=(k−1)c=2, so both triangles are equilateral.
steps: For smaller side s, √3s²/4=4√3 gives s=4.
The larger side is 6, with area √3·36/4.
